newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall after economic reports.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall after economic reports.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Monday after stronger-than-expected economic figures made stock and bond investors nervous about a possible pickup in inflation.

Shortly after 1:50 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 32.19 points at 7,298.85. But in the broader market, advancing issues led decliners by a 14-10 margin as more than 275 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index, which also dipped in early trading, rose 0.22 point to 1,400.54.

Bonds were little changed after an earlier slump sparked by a rise in the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index. The NAPM index posted a 57.1 reading in May, compared with a forecast 53.9 and a 54.2 reading in April.

The data halted a rally in the inflation-sensitive bond market, which had been initially assured by a report that consumer spending rose a scant 0.1 percent in April, its slowest rate in seven months. It also derailed an early rise in stocks.
"The market is getting over jitters created by the NAPM report," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
Johnson said the most disturbing part of the report was a rise in an index that measures the time it takes suppliers to fill orders.

"This is a key leading indicator of the economy and inflation and is watched very closely by the Federal Reserve," he said. "A rise in this index is bad news for deliveries and could mean upward pressure on prices before long."

Tom Carpenter, managing director and chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc, said the Dow industrials would have been up 50 points if the NAPM index had not been so strong. He cited the Dow's recent strength.
"But intermediate-term, I would not read too much into that 57.1 number," he said. "To some degree, it shows a snap back from the recent auto strikes and poor weather in the Upper Midwest."
The yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was unchanged at 6.91 percent.
Nasdaq was firm, helped by strength in technology stocks like Microsoft Corp., up 1-1/4 at 125-1/4, and Dell Corp., which was up 2 at 114-1/2.
PepsiCo stock was also active after the company said it would create a separate unit for its $6 billion-a-year bottling operations. Its shares were up 1-3/8 at 38-1/8.

Tobacco company stocks dipped after a Florida judge denied two motions sought by the industry in a secondhand smoke lawsuit. Philip Morris Cos. Inc. was off 1-1/8 at 42-7/8 and RJ Reynolds was off 3/4 at 31-5/8.
The American Stock Exchange index added 1.69 to 607.07.
